market.title: EU Instant Payments Mandate: Compliance Deadlines and VoP Impact
market.summary_short: European banks are facing critical deadlines for implementing the EU Instant Payments Regulation, requiring them to offer instant credit transfers in EUR. A key component is the mandatory Verification of Payee (VoP) to combat fraud.
market.summary_detail: The EU Instant Payments Regulation, which entered into force in April 2024, mandates that all payment service providers (PSPs) in the Eurozone must offer instant credit transfers in EUR. PSPs in the Eurozone must be able to *receive* instant payments by January 2025 and *send* them by January 2026. For non-Eurozone EU member states, these deadlines are extended by two years. A crucial aspect of the regulation is the mandatory Verification of Payee (VoP), requiring PSPs to check if the beneficiary's name matches the account number before a payment is executed, significantly enhancing fraud prevention. This regulation aims to modernize the European payment landscape, making transactions faster, more efficient, and safer for both consumers and corporates.
key_points: Eurozone PSPs must receive instant payments by Jan 2025, send by Jan 2026.
Non-Eurozone EU states have a two-year extension on these deadlines.
Mandatory Verification of Payee (VoP) is a core fraud prevention measure.
Regulation aims for faster, more efficient, and safer EUR transactions.
market.rbi_cash_management: This regulation is highly relevant for RBI CMIplus, as it directly impacts the payment services offered to corporates in CEE, including Eurozone and non-Eurozone EU countries. RBI must ensure its platform and network banks comply with instant payment capabilities and VoP requirements, providing seamless and secure real-time payments for its clients.

market.title: PSD3 Proposals Advance: Strengthening Open Banking and Fraud Prevention
market.summary_short: The European Commission's proposals for PSD3 and the new Payment Services Regulation (PSR) are progressing, aiming to enhance open banking frameworks and combat payment fraud more effectively. These legislative changes will significantly impact how payment services are regulated across the EU.
market.summary_detail: The European Commission introduced proposals for PSD3 and a new Payment Services Regulation (PSR) in June 2023, with legislative discussions ongoing. These proposals aim to strengthen the existing Open Banking framework by improving data access, security, and customer control, building on the success of PSD2. A major focus is also on combating payment fraud, with measures like enhanced information sharing between banks and mandatory fraud reporting. PSD3 will likely streamline the licensing process for Payment Initiation Service Providers (PISPs) and Account Information Service Providers (AISPs), fostering greater competition and innovation. The new framework is expected to provide clearer rules for new payment methods and digital currencies, ensuring a robust and secure digital payment ecosystem.
key_points: PSD3 and PSR proposals aim to strengthen Open Banking and combat fraud.
Enhanced data access, security, and customer control are key Open Banking goals.
New measures include improved information sharing and mandatory fraud reporting.
Expected to streamline licensing for PISPs and AISPs, fostering innovation.

market.title: Corporates Struggle to Maximize ISO 20022 Data Benefits
market.summary_short: Despite the widespread adoption of ISO 20022 for interbank payments, many corporates are still struggling to fully leverage its rich data capabilities for their internal treasury processes. This limits potential benefits in reconciliation, liquidity management, and fraud detection.
market.summary_detail: While the SWIFT CBPR+ migration to ISO 20022 is largely complete for interbank payments, the corporate-to-bank space presents ongoing challenges. Many corporates continue to use legacy formats or only partially adopt ISO 20022, failing to exploit the structured and rich data it offers. This leads to missed opportunities for automated reconciliation, improved liquidity forecasting, and enhanced fraud analytics. Treasury departments need to invest in upgrading their ERP and TMS systems to fully ingest and process the extended data fields, moving beyond basic payment execution to strategic data utilization. Banks are increasingly offering services to help corporates unlock these benefits, emphasizing the need for collaboration to realize the full potential of the ISO 20022 standard.

regulatory.title: VoP Matching Challenges: Standardisation and Accuracy Issues
regulatory.summary_short: The EBA Instant Payments Practitioners Group (IPG) highlights key challenges impacting the accuracy and quality of Verification of Payee (VoP) matching checks. These issues include a lack of standardised name-matching logic and limitations in name field lengths.
regulatory.summary_detail: The EBA Instant Payments Practitioners Group (IPG) has released an insight note detailing the significant pain points affecting the accuracy and overall quality of Verification of Payee (VoP) matching checks. The report identifies several critical challenges, such as the absence of a harmonised, pan-European name-matching logic, restrictions on name field lengths, and limitations related to virtual accounts. These issues can lead to discrepancies and hinder the effectiveness of VoP, which is a crucial fraud prevention tool mandated by the Instant Payments Regulation (IPR) and a key component of the broader Payment Services Regulation (PSR) and PSD3 framework. Addressing these challenges is vital for ensuring robust fraud detection and seamless instant payment processing.
key_points: Lack of standardised name-matching logic impacts VoP accuracy.
Name field length restrictions create data matching issues.
Limitations with virtual accounts pose challenges for VoP.
VoP is a critical fraud prevention tool under IPR/PSD3.
regulatory.rbi_cash_management: RBI's CMIplus needs to evaluate its current VoP implementation and future plans against these identified pain points, particularly regarding name matching logic and handling of virtual accounts for corporate payments. Proactive engagement with industry initiatives for standardisation is recommended to ensure robust fraud prevention and compliance.
